outcomes.statement: Group Admins see, on SCR-usage (/uso), per-person last activity and days inactive for their companies against a lag-aware data-through date, with company and 30/60/90 window filters, active/flagged/no-data metric cards, window and state badges, and the ~3-day freshness banner.
outcomes.demo: Seed two companies with activity at varied ages and a vendor account synced three days ago: /uso as group_admin lists only own-company people, days inactive counts from the data-through date (a person last active on the last synced day shows 0, not 3), the 30/60/90 filter changes the badge set and metric cards, people with no activity count as no data; a non-group_admin role is refused.

outcomes.statement: Group Admins select inactive people on SCR-usage and propose reclamation in one audited batch with an optional note, creating at most one pending ReclamationProposal per open assignment.
outcomes.demo: Select three flagged people and submit a note: three pending proposals with the note and proposed_by = the admin exist, one audit entry per proposal; resubmitting the same selection creates none; a person from another company in the payload is rejected; a non-group_admin role is refused.

outcomes.statement: An audited daily inactivity job sets flagged_inactive on the anchor LicenseRequest of every open assignment whose person trips the selected window against the lag-aware data-through date, without flagging people whose apparent inactivity is only the analytics lag.
outcomes.demo: Given activity ending 31 days before data-through for one person and 29 days for another, the job flags only the first person's anchor request active->flagged_inactive with a RequestTransition and audit entry; a rerun changes nothing; a person inactive only because of the 3-day lag is not flagged; another company's rows are untouched.

uncertainties.resolution: US-026 (with children US-070/US-071) has a terminal done event and is dev_done; activity_record carries activity_date and synced_at. Recorded as a resolved prerequisite, not a blocked_by dependency.

uncertainties.statement: BR-16 has no text in the repo; window, lag and flag ownership are inferred from 03_cx_journeys.md:162 and 04_er_model.md:366-388.
uncertainties.resolution: Policy rulings P1 (lag-aware data-through date), P2 (idempotency via the existing partial unique, no migration) and P3 (daily job flags at 30 days, no auto-proposals, un-flag on renewed activity) are requested from Francisco with the partition; nous reconciles BR-16 text in the canonical specs. The child uncertainties carry the budget.

uncertainties.statement: The parent exceeds execution limits (750 min > 320, five scopes, five acceptance flows, 24 files, three primary outcomes).
uncertainties.resolution: Partitioned into three vertical children of 260, 230 and 260 minutes; every parent AC is assigned and duplicated coverage carries a rationale. US-028 keeps approve/dismiss, suppression after dismissal, offboarding and /reclamaciones.

partitions.title: Usage surface: lag-aware inactivity per person on SCR-usage
partitions.outcome: Group Admins see, on SCR-usage (/uso), per-person last activity and days inactive for their companies against a lag-aware data-through date, with company and 30/60/90 window filters, active/flagged/no-data metric cards, window and state badges, and the ~3-day freshness banner.
partitions.demo: Seed two companies with activity at varied ages and a vendor account synced three days ago: /uso as group_admin lists only own-company people, days inactive counts from the data-through date (a person last active on the last synced day shows 0, not 3), the 30/60/90 filter changes the badge set and metric cards, people with no activity count as no data; a non-group_admin role is refused.

uncertainties.statement: No spec defines the data-through date used to absorb the ~3-day analytics lag (BR-16 has no text in the repo).
uncertainties.resolution: Pending Francisco's policy ruling P1: days inactive = data_through - last activity_date, where data_through is the latest activity_date synced for the person's vendor account (fallback: evaluation date - 3 days when the account has no sync). One pure domain function owns window and lag math and is shared with the flagging job; it carries property-based tests (monotone in last activity, window thresholds exact at 30/60/90).

uncertainties.statement: Existing inactive-candidate queries (pool-repository.ts:97, read-repository.ts:401) use wall-clock evaluation dates without lag.
uncertainties.resolution: The usage repository is new and uses the shared lag function; the two existing queries are left unchanged (their consumers are other stories) and the divergence is recorded as a deviation for a follow-up.

partitions.cross_cutting_rationale: AC1 is split: this child delivers the screen's filters, metric cards, last-active and badges; the batch proposal is the propose child. AC2 is split: this child applies the lag to displayed windows; the flagging child applies the same function to the state flag.

partitions.title: Batch reclamation proposals from SCR-usage
partitions.outcome: Group Admins select inactive people on SCR-usage and propose reclamation in one audited batch with an optional note, creating at most one pending ReclamationProposal per open assignment.
partitions.demo: Select three flagged people and submit a note: three pending proposals with the note and proposed_by = the admin exist, one audit entry per proposal; resubmitting the same selection creates none; a person from another company in the payload is rejected; a non-group_admin role is refused.

uncertainties.statement: The screen spec submits client_request_id but reclamation_proposal has no such column.
uncertainties.resolution: Pending Francisco's policy ruling P2: idempotency comes from the existing partial UNIQUE on pending proposals per assignment (V20260725180000:17) via insert-on-conflict-do-nothing; client_request_id is accepted and logged in the audit entry but not persisted; no migration.

Gate on group_admin with company:write and companyScope; wrap in withAudit and register the action in audited-actions-enforcement. Deciding proposals, dismissal suppression and /reclamaciones stay with US-028.

partitions.cross_cutting_rationale: AC1 is split: this child delivers the batch 'Proponer reclamación' action and modal on the surface the usage-surface child built.

partitions.title: Daily inactivity flagging of anchor license requests
partitions.outcome: An audited daily inactivity job sets flagged_inactive on the anchor LicenseRequest of every open assignment whose person trips the selected window against the lag-aware data-through date, without flagging people whose apparent inactivity is only the analytics lag.
partitions.demo: Given activity ending 31 days before data-through for one person and 29 days for another, the job flags only the first person's anchor request active->flagged_inactive with a RequestTransition and audit entry; a rerun changes nothing; a person inactive only because of the 3-day lag is not flagged; another company's rows are untouched.

uncertainties.statement: No spec states who sets flagged_inactive or against which window; 04_er_model.md:366 implies a job (proposed_by is null when the inactivity job proposes).
uncertainties.resolution: Pending Francisco's policy ruling P3: a daily inactivityFlagging schedule entry after analyticsSync (pg-boss runtime) flags at the 30-day window; the 60/90 windows are display filters only; the job does not create proposals (proposals stay admin-initiated in this story); un-flagging on renewed activity (flagged_inactive->active) is included because the lifecycle allows it.

uncertainties.statement: Concurrent job runs or a manual transition racing the job.
uncertainties.resolution: Transition with a conditional UPDATE on the current state (state = 'active') inside one transaction with the RequestTransition insert; real-DB integration test proves rerun and race idempotence.

partitions.cross_cutting_rationale: AC2 is split: this child applies the shared lag function delivered by usage-surface to the state flag. AC3 is wholly here.
